question: What age can my child join Scouting?
answer: Scouting Ireland welcomes young people from age 6 onwards. Our Beaver section takes children aged 6–8, Cubs are 8–11, Scouts are 11–15, and Ventures are 15–18. We recommend contacting us a term before your child reaches the minimum age so we can get them on the waiting list and introduce them to the section.

question: What does membership cost?
answer: Annual membership fees with 1st Meath Dunboyne are typically in the range of €80–€120 per year, depending on the section. This covers Scouting Ireland registration, insurance, and the general programme. Camps and special activities may have additional costs. We operate a bursary system for families who need financial support, please speak with a leader in confidence.

question: Do I need to buy a uniform?
answer: Yes, all members wear the Scouting Ireland uniform appropriate to their section. Uniforms are purchased through the Scouting Ireland online shop or at the Scout Shop in Dublin. We encourage purchasing second-hand where possible, we maintain a swap shop of outgrown uniforms that leaders can help you access.

question: Is scouting safe? What safeguarding measures are in place?
answer: Child safety is our absolute priority. All 1st Meath Dunboyne adult leaders are vetted by the National Vetting Bureau and hold current Scouting Ireland Child Protection Training and An Garda Síochána clearance. Our group has a Child Safeguarding Statement and a designated Safeguarding Representative. Scouting Ireland's comprehensive safeguarding framework applies to all activities. We follow a two-adult rule at all times, meaning no leader is ever alone with a young person.

question: What happens if my child has additional needs?
answer: Scouting Ireland is committed to being an inclusive organisation. We welcome young people of all abilities and needs, and work to adapt our programme wherever possible. If your child has additional needs, we encourage you to speak with us before they join so we can plan appropriately. Many of our leaders have additional training in inclusion and special educational needs.

question: How can I volunteer as an adult leader?
answer: We are always looking for enthusiastic adults to join our leadership team. No prior scouting experience is necessary, we will train you. All leaders complete Scouting Ireland's volunteer training programme and garda vetting process. Leaders must be 18 or over. If you're interested, please fill in the Volunteer form on our Join page, or email secretarydunboynescouts@gmail.com and a leader will be in touch.
